Root.value.semantic: controlled value; with `multiple` it is an array. No `selectedKey`/`selectedKeys` equivalent.

Root.items.semantic: optional item registry; when set, <Value> renders the selected label instead of the raw value.

Root.itemToStringLabel / itemToStringVal.semantic: object values -> display label / form-submission string. `{value,label}` shapes auto-resolve.

Root.isItemEqualToValue.semantic: custom value equality for object values.

Root.open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange /.semantic: controlled + uncontrolled popup state; onOpenChangeComplete fires after animations.

Root.modal.semantic: true locks page scroll and blocks outside pointer interaction (touch: blocks taps, keeps scroll unless popup spans nearly full viewport).

Root.highlightItemOnHover.semantic: false lets CSS :hover be distinguished from data-highlighted focus.

Root.actionsRef.semantic: imperative unmount after externally controlled close animations.

Trigger.nativeButton.semantic: set false when `render` swaps the button for a non-button element.

Value.placeholder.semantic: renders and marks the value with data-placeholder. children may be a formatting function.

Item.label.semantic: text used for keyboard typeahead matching; defaults to item text content.

Item.nativeButton.semantic: Item renders a div by default.

Positioner.alignItemWithTrigger.semantic: DEFAULT TRUE: overlaps the popup with the trigger so the selected item's text aligns with the value text; mouse input only, auto-disabled when space is short. Popup then reports data-side='none'. Set false for a normal React-Aria-like dropdown.

Positioner.side / align / sideOffset / a.semantic: same anchoring contract as every other Base UI Positioner.

Positioner.anchor / arrowPadding / colli.type: Element|VirtualElement|Ref|fn / number / object / Boundary / Padding / boolean / 'absolute'|'fixed' / boolean

Popup.finalFocus.semantic: where focus goes on close (default: trigger / previously focused element).

ScrollUpArrow / ScrollDownArrow.semantic: hover-scroll affordances; not rendered for touch input; state data-visible.

dataAttributes: Trigger: data-popup-open (popup open), data-pressed, data-disabled, data-readonly, data-required, data-popup-side ('top'|'bottom'|'left'|'right'|'inline-end'|'inline-start'|null), data-valid, data-invalid, data-dirty, data-touched, data-filled, data-focused (Field.Root), data-placeholder (no value)
Positioner: data-open, data-closed, data-anchor-hidden, data-side, data-align
Popup: data-open, data-closed, data-starting-style, data-ending-style, data-side, data-align
Arrow: data-open, data-closed, data-side, data-align, data-uncentered
ScrollUpArrow/ScrollDownArrow: data-starting-style, data-ending-style, data-direction ('up'|'down'), data-visible, data-side
List / Group / GroupLabel / Separator / Label / ItemText: none
renderProp: Every part extends BaseUIComponentProps: { render?: ReactElement | ((props: HTMLProps, state: <Part>.State) => ReactElement); className?: string | ((state) => string|undefined); style?: CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties|undefined) }. `render` replaces the rendered element (e.g. render={<Button/>}) and receives merged props. Authoring your own primitive: useRender(params) from '@base-ui/react/use-render' (params: render, ref, state, stateAttributesMapping, props, enabled, defaultTagName; state props are converted to data-* automatically). Merging external props into a Base UI part: mergeProps(a,b,...) / mergePropsN([...]) from '@base-ui/react/merge-props' — rightmost wins except event handlers (merged, invoked right-to-left; a right handler can stop earlier ones via event.preventBaseUIHandler()), className concatenates right-to-left, style objects merge rightmost-wins; `ref` is NOT merged.
controlled: Value: `value` (controlled) vs `defaultValue` (uncontrolled), change callback `onValueChange(value, eventDetails)`. Popup: `open` vs `defaultOpen` (default false), callbacks `onOpenChange(open, eventDetails)` and `onOpenChangeComplete(open)`. Imperative: `actionsRef` -> { unmount }. No `isOpen`/`onOpenChange`-style React Aria names.
formIntegration: Root renders a hidden `<input type=hidden form name value>` (verified in select/root/SelectRoot.mjs) carrying the serialized value; `name` identifies the field, `form` associates it with an external form, `inputRef` exposes the input element, `itemToStringValue` controls the submitted string. `required` participates in constraint validation; `readOnly`/`disabled` propagate to the control state. Field.Root adds data-valid/data-invalid/data-dirty/data-touched/data-filled/data-focused.
keyboard: List navigation (internal useListNavigation): ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the highlight, Home/End jump to first/last (they do NOT move the text caret for a typeable combobox, but Select is not typeable so no caret conflict); no PageUp/PageDown handling anywhere in the package. Typeahead: printable characters match item `label` or item text, session reset after TYPEAHEAD_RESET_MS = 500 ms, space continues an in-progress session (floating-ui-react useTypeahead). Enter/Space select the highlighted item; Escape closes and returns focus (useDismiss); Tab moves focus out; modal=true traps focus via FloatingFocusManager. Docs explicitly state Select is not filterable aside from 'basic keyboard typeahead functionality to find items by focusing and highlighting them'.
notableDifferences: Prop naming: `disabled`/`readOnly`/`required` instead of isDisabled/isReadOnly/isRequired; `multiple` instead of selectionMode='multiple'.

No `<Select>` single element: composition is Root > Label + Trigger(Value, Icon) + Portal > Positioner > Popup > List > (ScrollUpArrow, Item(ItemIndicator, ItemText), ScrollDownArrow). React Aria's `SelectValue` maps to `Select.Value` with a `placeholder` prop (and data-placeholder), not a render-prop `children`.

Positioner default `alignItemWithTrigger=true` deliberately overlaps popup and trigger (data-side='none' on the popup); a migration that expects a normal detached dropdown MUST set `alignItemWithTrigger={false}`.

State is exposed only as data-* attributes (data-selected / data-highlighted / data-disabled / data-placeholder ...), not as render-prop state objects; React Aria's data-selected/data-focused naming partially overlaps but data-highlighted replaces 'focused' for roving highlight, and there is no data-focus-visible/data-hovered.

Item registration: options are registered by rendering `Select.Item` (value + optional label); the optional `items` prop on Root only powers label lookup for <Value> and typed generics — there is no `<Item key>`-less API and no `Item textValue` (it is `label`).
Object values are first-class: `isItemEqualToValue`, `itemToStringLabel`, `itemToStringValue` replace React Aria's `getKey`/`textValue` conventions.
Popup is portal+positioner+popup with `data-starting-style`/`data-ending-style` for enter/exit animation, instead of React Aria's transition state props.
Multi-select value is `Value[]` (empty array semantics differ from React Aria's Key[]); no `onSelectionChange`.
